assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window: a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector established a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos beyond atmospheric backgrounds, then pointed to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources. Clear, original, instrumentally demanding and with lasting impact on multi-messenger astronomy and cosmic-ray origin.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the concept and the IceCube programme; Karle was central to the detector and ice-instrumentation development; Spiering is credited as an early pioneer of neutrino telescopes (Baikal, AMANDA). Precursor efforts (DUMAND, Baikal, ANTARES) and a large collaboration make a three-person split imperfect, and I rely on my general knowledge for the exact roles.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the diffuse flux has been confirmed across several event samples and analyses, and the source associations have grown over a decade. Timing is good, though individual source identifications remain at moderate significance.
uncertainties: Fair weighting between Halzen, Karle, Spiering and unlisted founders of neutrino telescopy is unresolved.
Source-level evidence (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) is still at moderate significance and not independently confirmed by other telescopes.
I work in astroparticle physics; I know the field but declare no recorded tie to these individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle was followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene. This launched moire quantum matter and twistronics, with a clean theory-meets-experiment narrative and broad impact.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model and the Jarillo-Herrero group experiments are the decisive pair of contributions, so the three listed names map well onto the story. Others, notably the Columbia and Manchester groups and co-authors, have claims, but a prize to these three is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years since the 2018 experiments; replicated by many groups, with fractional Chern insulators, orbital magnetism and superconductivity extensively studied. Interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still debated, though the core discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity in the moire system is not settled.
Credit relative to other early twisted-graphene theory and experiment is not fully resolved.
Early sample-dependence and reproducibility issues were reported, as I recall.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect from spin-orbit coupling in graphene and the Z2 topological classification, followed by the observation of edge transport in HgTe quantum wells. A conceptually deep, widely influential field with strong theory-experiment connection.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the foundational theory and Z2 invariant; Molenkamp led the HgTe experimental realization. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe route and are not in this credit set, so an allocation problem remains if the HgTe link is emphasized. Fu, Moore, Hsieh and Hasan on 3D insulators are also outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: confirmed across many materials and platforms for nearly two decades; the 2005-2007 results are well established. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Omission of Zhang (deceased) and of Bernevig, Hughes as HgTe predictors.
Whether the 3D topological insulator work should be part of the same prize.
Overlap with candidate B012, which credits partly different people for related physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Invention of the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and its development to the 10^-18 fractional-uncertainty level. Foundational for precision metrology, tests of fundamental constants and prospective redefinition of the second, with clear originality and strong instrumental impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group brought it to record accuracy; both are plausible laureates. Hall and Hansch were already recognized in 2005 for the frequency comb that enables the clocks, and other groups (e.g., NIST, PTB, Lemonde) have secondary claims.
assessment.maturity: The idea is two decades old, performance has been confirmed by independent labs, and the second redefinition is being considered; maturity is high though the practical redefinition is not yet complete.
uncertainties: Whether the clock work is regarded as sufficiently distinct from the frequency-comb prize.
Role of other groups developing parallel lattice-clock platforms.
Timing relative to the formal redefinition of the second.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical proposal of quantum computation with trapped ions and its experimental realization with ions, plus the broader programme of quantum simulation with controlled atoms. Foundational and lasting, though part of the field was recognized through the 2012 prize to Wineland and Haroche.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the ion-trap gate scheme, and Blatt led much of its experimental realization in Innsbruck. Bloch (optical-lattice simulation) is dropped because the combined candidate looks like two prizes in one; Wineland has already been recognized, and others (Monroe, Wineland, Kimble) overlap.
assessment.maturity: High: several platforms now implement the ideas, and results have been independently replicated worldwide. Recognition would be timely given quantum technology's growth, albeit competing with the 2022 and 2025 quantum prizes.
uncertainties: The candidate is compound; I choose the trapped-ion core and leave out Bloch's lattice work.
Overlap with prior quantum prizes may reduce novelty.
Credit versus Monroe and Wineland is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, especially H.E.S.S., opened the TeV gamma-ray sky and produced the first resolved images of supernova-remnant shells and a large Galactic source population. As an instrumentalist, I regard this as an excellent combination of technique and discovery that supports cosmic-ray origin studies.
assessment.attribution: Aharonian provided theoretical interpretation and led early HEGRA/H.E.S.S. science; Hofmann led the H.E.S.S. collaboration. The technique itself came from Weekes (Whipple Crab detection) and Hillas (shower imaging), neither listed here, so the supplied credit cannot support a fair prize on its own.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the field is firmly established, with H.E.S.S., MAGIC, VERITAS and now CTAO. Recognition would not be premature, but the historical credit problem may cause the committee to hesitate.
uncertainties: Weekes and Hillas are missing from the credited names, which undermines fair attribution.
Whether the prize should reward the technique or the discoveries.
I work in neighbouring gamma-ray instrumentation, so I am cautious not to overweight the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz stochastic gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays, with the Hellings-Downs angular correlation signature, opens the nanohertz band, possibly sourced by supermassive black-hole binaries. Scientifically important and instrumentally elegant.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA, CPTA and IPTA, and pioneers of pulsar timing; the listed four-name set is not obviously complete. I choose three, but an allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Premature: 2023 evidence is around 3-4 sigma for the correlation and the astrophysical source is not settled. Independent datasets agree qualitatively, though a definitive detection and cleaner interpretation are still awaited.
uncertainties: Significance of the Hellings-Downs signature is below the conventional discovery threshold, as I recall.
Origin of the signal (supermassive black-hole binaries vs. new physics) is open.
Which pulsar-timing pioneers and collaborations deserve credit is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provided the architecture for strong coupling and dispersive readout of superconducting qubits, underpinning modern superconducting quantum processors. High impact and clean physics, with a natural link to the Nobel-recognized circuit quantum phenomena of 2025.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first experimental demonstrations; this configuration is clear. Overlap with the 2025 laureates and with Nakamura and others on qubit development remains to be weighed.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of widespread reproduction and use; but the very recent prize in superconducting circuits may make a second award in this area untimely.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize may reduce the case for a second superconducting-circuit award.
Credit relative to Nakamura and others for qubit development is unclear.
Whether quantum-computing applications are judged as physics discovery or engineering.
